subject: Turkish alphabet blackboard
title: What If a Country Changed Its Alphabet Overnight? Turkey Did in 1928

scenes.text: What if your country changed its alphabet overnight? Turkey did in 1928. Three months, done.
On August 9th, 1928, Atatürk unveiled the new Latin letters in an Istanbul park, then toured the country teaching them himself.
The law passed on November 1st: 29 letters replaced Arabic script. Newspapers had until December 1st to switch.
Atatürk had refused a five-year phase-in. His words: this will be done in three months or never.
On January 1st, 1929, state offices switched and the Nation's Schools opened for adults. Over a million enrolled in the first year.
Literacy was 10.5 percent in 1927. By 1935 it had doubled to 20.4 percent. Grandparents kept the old letters for decades.

description:
What if a country swapped its alphabet almost overnight? Turkey's Alphabet Law of 1 November 1928 replaced Arabic script with a 29-letter Latin alphabet; newspapers switched by December 1928 and state offices by 1 January 1929, when the Nation's Schools opened to teach adults.
More than a million people enrolled in the first year. Literacy rose from 10.5 percent in the 1927 census to 20.4 percent in 1935.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Three letters were dropped completely: q, w and x. Could your country relearn how to write in three months? And what should we run through next?
